Definition: from G3152 and G3004; an idle (i.e. senseless or mischievous) talker, i.e. a wrangler:--vain talker.
BiblicalUsage: A vain talker is someone whose words are empty and unruly, and Paul warns Titus that there are many of them, especially among those who insist on the old law.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the warning still stands: a teacher is known by whether his words build up the church or only fill the air, and the church must be able to tell the difference.
